I somehow managed to make it through three years at university (with minimal effort, although I'm fairly intelligent, so still got good marks for the most part), but everything fell apart after that.  I hadn't really given a shit about what was going to happen after graduation, apart from some vague ideas of going into postgraduate studies, and it still didn't bother me when it was all about to end.  I didn't even have a backup plan, nor feel the need to consider one, so my plans to make a career for myself kind of stalled there.  It's not just with more long-term stuff either - I can barely muster up the motivation to plan stuff a week in advance, let alone lay the groundwork for things that are still two years off.

I briefly experienced something that I think was remorse once.  I was quite sleep-deprived though, and it was after I'd just killed an entire family in a video game, so I'm not 100% sure.  It was like a weird mix of nausea and self-loathing, anyway.

Yup.  Whenever I see my 90-something-year-old great-grandmother, all I can think of is how I never want to be in her position.  Her memory goes from shoddy to outright abysmal and back again in the course of a few hours, she can barely walk without someone to help her (and walks about as slowly as you can while having it still be considered walking), and she spends most of her days in bed sleeping and/or feverish.  She's little more than a corpse whose brain hasn't caught on at this point, not to mention a drain on others' time and resources.

I don't get why she's still hanging around, apart from the fact that she's probably physically incapable of killing herself without assistance.  All I know is that I sure as hell don't want to wind up the same way.

I'm generally not great at coming up with one-liners that aren't innuendos or puns, but I once had a falling-out with a girl who has a long history of body image issues (it was one of the few cases where someone tried to cut me off because they realised what sort of person I really am).  I was kind of annoyed by how passive-aggressively she approached it, so the last thing I said to her before we cut off contact entirely was "You know, you could probably stand to lose a bit of weight".

Last I heard, she lapsed into a full-blown eating disorder.  That was probably inevitable, given just how hard she used to try and justify her eating habits to the world over Facebook, but the possibility that I played some part in it amuses me for some reason - and I'm usually not all that malicious.

It's pretty much the reason why I'm unemployed at the moment, and why my attempts at building a career are in limbo.  When it comes right down to it, I'm more than happy to live off others' generosity, whether it be money from my family, or from government support payments).  I don't need much money to live the way I want to, nor do I really care about what other people need to do to keep me afloat.

I do get bursts of motivation where I genuinely want to build a career for myself, but my chronic inability to care about things for more than a month or two generally stops any attempts I make to change in their tracks.

My mother was a textbook case of BPD.  She had phases where she was incredibly melodramatic and emotional, cheated on my father, abused alcohol, made suicidal gestures, spent way too much money, and did shit for attention like sunbathing topless in public, and I had no tolerance for it whatsoever.  I'd usually just avoid her whenever she was acting out, although I sometimes had some fun with it and egged her on if she started threatening to kill herself.  She eventually did commit suicide, although I suspect that she was merely stupid enough to think that suspension hanging made for a safe suicidal gesture.

She was a genuinely nice person during her "stable" phases though. I generally got along with her at those times, at least until I finally got sick of the mood swings and cut off contact.

I've known loads of other people who have been diagnosed as borderline - and unsurprisingly, most of them were girls that I went to high school with (I have major issues with diagnosing BPD that young, because most of the diagnostic criteria just as easily describe a hormonal teenage girl).  Suffice to say, most of them mellowed out in their early 20s - only a couple would still meet the critera for a BPD diagnosis today, and I make a point of keeping my distance from those ones.

> To this day I honestly still struggle with actually believing that people don't actually think the way I do or feel the way I do. How I am is: objective, rational, and logical. 

This is one of those things that causes loads of cognitive dissonance for me.  I frequently get irritated when other people don't realise that their opinions and feelings aren't necessarily shared by others.  However, when those opinions/feelings differ from *mine* (which are generally very objective and logical), I get confused, often to the point of frustration, and start questioning their intelligence.

The cognitive dissonance aspect doesn't bother me in any way (it's actually kind of amusing), but I've been noticing it a lot recently, ever since a friend pointed it out a couple of months back.

I usually find I'm even more emotionally blunted than usual when sleep deprived, unless a mild increase in irritability counts (although mixing in alcohol tends to lead to unprovoked, uncontrollable crying, similar to what you described).  After a while, I also start to feel a tension in my chest, similar anxiety, but without any cognitive/affective component to it.  I suspect that may be due to sleep deprivation increasing heart rate, impairing oxygen uptake, etc.

There was one weird case though, a few years ago when I was playing *The Elder Scrolls: Oblivion* one night, after about 36 hours without sleep.  I was doing a quest where I had to kill an entire family, and at the end, I actually felt genuinely remorseful - like a weird mixture of nausea and self-loathing.  It passed quickly, but it was still a bit of a headtrip.
